title: Proactive failover sentinels and circuit-breaker matrix for region/tier routing
creator: Anjali Rao
description: Design and implement a unified set of automatic fallback triggers (429s, timeouts, and error-rate thresholds) and a configurable circuit-breaker matrix that is aware of region, customer tier, and model-variant compatibility. The goal is to minimize customer-visible failures while preserving model quality and cost targets. This work covers: 1) sentinel definitions and per-route sliding-window metrics, 2) open/half-open/closed circuit transitions with backoff multipliers, 3) tier- and region-aware thresholds and failover ordering, 4) probe/quilting strategy for half-open state, and 5) dashboarding and synthetic canary knobs for gradual rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinels implemented for: 429 rate, request timeout rate, response error rate (5xx/invalid-response), and p95 latency regressions.
Per-route and per-region sliding-window logic with configurable window (default 2m) and min-sample thresholds is available in config.
Circuit breaker states (CLOSED / OPEN / HALF_OPEN) with exponential backoff and probe behavior implemented in routing runtime.
Fallback ordering respects region affinity and tier policies: prefer same-region cheaper model-variant, then cross-region failover if allowed by route policy.
Operator-visible dashboards and an alert rule template are added; runbooks updated with example thresholds and triage steps.
Automated integration test that injects synthetic 429s/timeouts verifies fallback path and that requests are not amplified during recovery (no thundering herd).
technical_notes: We will implement a two-layer approach: local fast-sentinels in the serving runtime for immediate per-node protection, and a central decision engine for coordinated circuit state for routing clusters. Sentinels use an EWMA-smoothed sliding window with minSamples=200 by default and configurable windowMs (default 120000). Triggers: 1) 429 trigger: if (429_count / total_requests) >= 0.01 over window AND total_requests >= minSamples -> mark sentinel=TRIPPED. 2) timeout trigger: if (timeout_count / total_requests) >= 0.005 over window -> TRIPPED. 3) error trigger: if (5xx_count / total_requests) >= 0.02 over window -> TRIPPED. 4) latency regression: if p95_latency >= slo_p95 + 200ms for two consecutive windows -> TRIPPED. These baseline thresholds are conservative; they are adjustable per-customer tier (enterprise tiers get wider thresholds for cross-region failover). Circuit breaker open duration baseOpenMs=30000, multiplied by 2^n on successive opens up to maxOpenMs=15m. Half-open behavior: allow N_probe=5 requests distributed across nodes; require k_success >= 4 to close. Probes should be sampled at controlled rate (not more than 0.5% of route QPS) and tagged so logs/metrics can be filtered. Recovery must prefer local model variants that preserve model family compatibility, otherwise downgrade quality levels according to the route policy. Use header X-RW-Routing-Decision for traceability. Use stable hashing to avoid sending probes to same instance repeatedly.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated behind 'rb_proactive_failover' and 'rb_circuit_matrix' per cluster. 2) Start with internal canary: 1% traffic in us-west-2 for non-critical routes for 24h with synthetic fault injection. 3) Expand to 10% with enterprise customers opted-in for 48h. 4) Enable default thresholds for all non-P0 routes and monitor. 5) After 2 weeks of stable telemetry, flip on for additional regions and adjust thresholds via dashboard. 6) Final step: automated threshold tuning experiment (opt-in) to recompute EWMA alpha and base thresholds per route based on historical SLOs.
